narrative.overview:
Gradelings shares one material kit—warm notebook paper, midnight slate ink, bright subject colours, rounded Fredoka UI type, and Andika for reading—across the product. That kit is applied at three different desks: the kids' arcade classroom (/play/), the parent's calm report desk (/parents/ and marketing), and the operator's flat console (/admin/). Same crayons; different volume.

Personality is kind, chunky, and clear. Play earns game juice (jelly, squash-and-stretch, critters, confetti). Parents get scanable trust without arcade chrome. Admin gets density and speed with flat controls—no mascots, no jelly. Never shame; never purple-SaaS generic; never sterile gray on play.

Visual anti-references (confirmed): arcade chrome on /parents/ or /admin/; sterile edtech gray on /play/; purple-gradient SaaS everywhere; critters on admin.
keyCharacteristics: One shared token kit; three surface densities (play / parents / admin)
Warm paper stage with soft pastel corner washes
Chunky press-down controls with a hard colour ledge (not soft drop shadows by default)
Jelly and critters only on play (and marketing brand moments); admin stays flat
Accessibility modes (contrast, roomy, dyslexia font, forced colours) are first-class, not afterthoughts

rules.name: The Three Desks Rule
rules.body: Shared colours; different saturation of expression. Play may flood with subject colour and juice. Parents stay paper + ink + one accent. Admin prefers slate borders, compact fills, and almost no rainbow.

rules.name: The Dark-on-Bright Rule
rules.body: Bright fills (help, good, nudge) use near-black text (#0f172a), never white.

rules.name: The Honest Accent Rule
rules.body: Nudge orange is kindness, not error theatre. Don’t invent a harsh error red as a new system primary without product need.

rules.name: The Read Font Rule
rules.body: Continuous reading (questions, stories, long parent copy) uses Andika (font-read). Fredoka is for chrome and short labels.

rules.name: The No Admin Typeface Rule
rules.body: /admin/ does not get a separate “ops” font. Density changes size and spacing, not family.

rules.name: The Touch Floor Rule
rules.body: Interactive targets stay at least 48px for kids and 44px elsewhere; CI device scripts enforce this.

rules.name: The Desk Density Rule
rules.body: Play = large, few choices. Parents = scannable sections. Admin = dense tables and tools. Same tokens; different packing.

rules.name: The Ledge-Not-Blur Rule
rules.body: Do not use soft/diffuse drop shadows for depth. Play and marketing sit on the colour ledge; parents and admin use flat borders. Prefer dimming the page behind a dialog over inventing a shadow elevation scale.

rules.name: The Jelly Desk Rule
rules.body: Jelly / squash-and-stretch belongs to /play/ (and brief marketing delight). Parents stay calm; admin stays flat. Always respect prefers-reduced-motion and calm mode.

rules.name: The Visible Edge Rule
rules.body: Borders are part of the character. Don’t replace ledge + border with shadow-only cards on play/marketing.

dos: Do reuse Warm Notebook Paper, Midnight Slate, and the help/good/nudge accents before inventing new greys or purples.
Do put juice (jelly, confetti, critter idle motion) on /play/ and light brand moments on marketing only.
Do keep admin flat, dense, and critter-free while still using Fredoka/Andika and the shared palette.
Do use dark text on bright fills; keep the 4px focus ring.
Do honour calm mode, reduced motion, contrast, roomy text, and dyslexia font switches.
donts: Don’t put arcade chrome, jelly, or mascots on /parents/ or /admin/.
Don’t make /play/ sterile, gray, or “serious SaaS.”
Don’t default to purple-to-indigo gradient themes or soft neumorphism.
Don’t use soft drop shadows for elevation—toy ledge or flat border only.
Don’t hard-code the product name; read APP_NAME from src/lib/brand.ts.
Don’t invent testimonials or treat sample quotes as real parents (see PRODUCT.md).
